attributes.protocol: Frozen model last-hidden-state embeddings, mean pooled. Logistic regression for eight classification tasks and mini-batch k-means for eight clustering tasks. Source paper Section 5.3. Current official gene-mteb implementation corroborates task identities but its commit is not proven identical to the paper evaluator. Exact dataset release, split hash, scored counts and evaluator commit are unreported in the paper. Do not substitute current mutable HF main for the original split.
attributes.source_locator: Table 3 (S5.T3), row Human-Virus-2, column DNABERT-2; Section 5.3 paragraphs S5.SS3.p2.1 and S5.SS3.p3.1

attributes.protocol: Retrospective evaluation of six CASP15 natural single-chain RNA targets; each task retains one named target. Artificially designed targets and RNA-protein complexes excluded. RNA sequence inputs without ions or other molecules. Paper Par13 selects the highest-performing of five candidates; Par51 describes five sampled-MSA runs for RhoFold+, one AlphaFold3 server run yielding five models, and five CASP15 models for the other methods. Figure 2h reports RMSD and sum of Z-scores for GDT-TS and TM-score. Metric-specific winning candidate identity, exact scoring-tool revision and RMSD atom selection remain unextracted. No target pooling or score recomputation.

comparison.metric_implementation: Sum of Z-scores for GDT-TS and TM-score

attributes.source_locator: fig2hi!I4; method fig2hi!A4; target fig2hi!I1; Fig. 2h caption; XML Par13–15 and Par51
attributes.candidate_selection: Highest-performing candidate as described in Par13; metric-specific candidate identity unreported.
attributes.adaptation: Source-labelled five-candidate CASP15 configuration; fine-tuning and exact checkpoints not established. No additional adaptation inferred.
attributes.evidence_overlap: Twelve per-target/metric observations per complete method belong to one six-target comparison setup. RMSD and cumulative Z-score reuse candidate predictions; CASP15 submissions quoted here are not new independent evidence.

name: Centrifuger v1.1.1-r309 on Mutated virus mock-community profiling against ground truth (Tisza et al. 2026 Table S9)
description: Published developer benchmark; transcribed, not reproduced.

comparison.dataset_version: Six mutated virus mock communities with bacterial and human background (Tisza et al. 2026)
comparison.population: Three communities of 90 random Virus Pathogen Database genomes and three of 60 genomes with at most one per family, mutated to 80%, 85%, 90%, 95%, 98% and 100% ANI; 10,000 InSilicoSeq NovaSeq read pairs per virus plus 50,000,000 reads from 100 bacterial genomes and the human genome
comparison.inputs: Synthetic NovaSeq read pairs (InSilicoSeq)
comparison.adaptation: Headline setting: minimum-hit-length 100, minimum score 0
comparison.metric_implementation: Strict truth uses the provenance lineage at each rank; capped truth caps the rank by ANI (98-100%: subspecies, 90-95%: species, 80-85%: genus). Profiles normalised to relative abundance per tool; means over the six communities.

limitations: Run by the developers of EsViritu, who chose each comparator's parameter grid and headline setting.
All tools queried the same Virus Pathogen Database (v3.2.4b), so reference content is held constant; real-world tools are usually run with their own databases.

description: SegmentNT human genome annotation evaluation of BPNet arch. on 3UTR: per-nucleotide annotation (auPRC), scored with Area under precision-recall curve.

attributes.protocol: Test chromosomes 20 and 21; validation chromosome 22; training remaining chromosomes. Test chunks with genes homologous to train/validation genes excluded using Ensembl BioMart accessed 2024-05-08; homologous distal regulatory elements not excluded. Ten test-set samplings with sliding windows beginning at different genomic starting positions. Mean plus reported standard deviation; not ten training seeds. Best validation checkpoint by average MCC across 14 elements. Per-nucleotide predictions pooled across test sequences separately for each genomic element. MCC and auPRC are separate metrics, not cross-element or cross-table pooled comparisons.

name: AlphaMissense: points-scale PP3/BP4 score intervals (Bergquist et al. 2025)
description: Published calibration; transcribed, not reproduced.

comparison.population: 11,834 missense variants from 1,914 genes; prior probability of pathogenicity 4.41% (gnomAD set)
comparison.inputs: Precomputed or author-generated scores of the tool for each variant
comparison.adaptation: None; thresholds fitted to the tool's scores
comparison.metric_implementation: Local posterior probability of pathogenicity estimated in a sliding score window on the ClinVar 2019 set with prior 0.0441; a threshold is the most lenient score at which the one-sided 95% bootstrap bound (10,000 iterations) of the local positive likelihood ratio still reaches the cut-off for that strength (2.406, 5.790, 33.53, 1,124; reciprocals for BP4)
comparison.aggregation: Pooled over variants in all genes

comparison.budget.note: Calibration of precomputed scores; no compute budget
